item.title: UPNG Chancellor to respond to Vice-Chancellor’s resignation
item.description: UPNG Chancellor Sir Robert Igara has told NBC News he will issue an official statement on Tuesday, following a council meeting. It follows the resignation of Vice-Chancellor Professor Ian Findlay.
item.content:encoded:
UPNG Chancellor Sir Robert Igara has told NBC News he will issue an official statement on Tuesday, following a council meeting.

It follows the resignation of Vice-Chancellor Professor Ian Findlay.

Professor Findlay resigned with immediate effect today, Monday, November 2, after 15 months in the position.

In his resignation letter, he said ongoing disagreements with the Chancellor over the governance and management of the university had made it difficult for him to continue.

He also accused the Chancellor of alleged bullying and disrespect, referring to their confrontation at a special council meeting on October 28.

Professor Findlay said he had made progress in improving the university's finances, academic standards, administration and student services during his time in office.

However, he raised concerns over a recent student riot and claims threats to his personal safety had forced him to leave the country.

He said he remained proud of the reforms achieved and hoped.

item.title: KPHL explains funding for State’s US$1.1 billion Papua LNG stake
item.description: Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited [KPHL] says the State’s US$1.1 billion investment in the Papua LNG Project will be funded through domestic borrowing and revenue from its existing PNG LNG investment, without direct funding from the National Budget. KPHL Chairman Ambassador Isaac Lupari said the funding covers the State’s 22.5 per cent equity stake in Papua LNG, not the total cost of developing the
item.content:encoded:
Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited [KPHL] says the State’s US$1.1 billion investment in the Papua LNG Project will be funded through domestic borrowing and revenue from its existing PNG LNG investment, without direct funding from the National Budget.

KPHL Chairman Ambassador Isaac Lupari said the funding covers the State’s 22.5 per cent equity stake in Papua LNG, not the total cost of developing the project.

He said US$300 million would come from a syndicated loan arranged by Bank South Pacific, while the remaining US$800 million would be generated from KPHL’s 15.1 per cent share in the PNG LNG Project between 2026 and 2032.

Mr Lupari clarified that the US$800 million was not currently available in cash but would be generated progressively over the construction period to meet the State’s share of project costs.

KPHL has already secured US$180 million for the first payment following a Final Investment Decision (FID). This forms part of the overall US$1.1 billion funding package.

Mr Lupari said the financing approach would avoid a direct National Budget allocation for the State’s equity contribution, allowing government funds to remain available for priorities such as health, education and infrastructure.

However, he said KPHL’s ability to provide dividends and other financial support to the Government would be limited during the financing period as the company prioritises project funding and debt repayments.

Mr Lupari said Papua LNG was expected to generate economic benefits during construction and production.

Construction spending on wages, local suppliers and contractors is expected to create business opportunities and support household incomes.

Once production begins, the project is expected to generate foreign exchange through LNG exports, along with taxes, royalties and other benefits for the country.

The State’s equity participation through KPHL is also expected to provide long-term investment returns.

However, he said the timing and value of these benefits would depend on the project reaching FID, successful construction, production performance, LNG prices, operating costs and debt repayments.

Mr Lupari also urged national leaders to ensure public statements about major resource projects were based on accurate information, warning that misleading comments could undermine investor confidence and efforts to secure future financing.

KPHL issued the statement on November 1, 2026.

item.title: Rufina Peter to lead Christian Democratic Party
item.description: Central Governor Rufina Peter is set to take charge of the Christian Democratic Party parliamentary leadership, following her appointment , over the weekend. Her appointment was made over the weekend as the party continues to develop its constitution, policy platform, membership structure and national organisation.
item.content:encoded:
Central Governor Rufina Peter is set to take charge of the Christian Democratic Party parliamentary leadership, following her appointment , over the weekend.

Her appointment was made over the weekend as the party continues to develop its constitution, policy platform, membership structure and national organisation.

Founded in 1990's, the Christian Democratic Party was established on a vision of contributing to the leadership and development of Papua New Guinea.

CDP interim president Davis Steven has welcomed Governor Peter's appointment.

In formally accepting her appointment, the Governor expressed gratitude for the opportunity, not only to uphold Christian values but also maintain integrity of institutions and addressing issues affecting the nation.

Meanwhile, People's National Congress Party leader Peter O'Neill said he was aware of Governor Peter's appointment and wished her well in the new role.

The CDP currently has no elected parliamentary leader in the 11th National Parliament.

Now with Governor Peter taking over the leadership, CDP hopes to change this and strengthen its presence in the country’s political landscape.

item.title: PNG and Fiji to formalise ICT cooperation
item.description: Papua New Guinea and Fiji are moving towards a formal agreement to strengthen cooperation in information and communications technology (ICT), following a four-day official visit by PNG's ICT Minister Robert Naguri to Suva. Minister Naguri returned to Port Moresby today after meetings with Fijian government ministers, senior officials and industry representatives to identify areas of cooperation be
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea and Fiji are moving towards a formal agreement to strengthen cooperation in information and communications technology (ICT), following a four-day official visit by PNG's ICT Minister Robert Naguri to Suva.

Minister Naguri returned to Port Moresby today after meetings with Fijian government ministers, senior officials and industry representatives to identify areas of cooperation between the two countries.

He said the visit was not a one-off engagement but the beginning of a stronger and more practical partnership in the ICT sector.

Minister Naguri has directed the Department of ICT, National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC], National Information and Communications Technology Authority [NICTA] and the PNG High Commission in Suva to follow up on the areas of cooperation identified during the visit.

He said both countries would work towards finalising a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] for consideration and signing at the earliest opportunity.

The proposed agreement will provide a framework for information-sharing, technical cooperation, institutional and human resource capacity-building, and joint initiatives across the ICT sector.

Minister Naguri said the discussions highlighted that PNG and Fiji shared similar challenges in ICT, as well as opportunities that could be developed through closer cooperation.

He also said the proposed partnership would be guided by the spirit of the Lakatoi Declaration and complement wider regional priorities under the Pacific Islands Forum infrastructure agenda.

During his visit, Minister Naguri met with his Fijian counterpart, Minister for Policing and Communications Ioane Naivalurua, who formally invited him to Fiji.

The Minister also met with Pacific Islands Forum Secretary-General Baron Waqa and his management team.

His programme included participation in a ministerial panel discussion at Fiji's National Cybersecurity and Resilience Convention, as well as discussions with the Israeli Ambassador to Fiji and Pacific Island states on opportunities for cooperation in ICT and agriculture.

He also visited the Fijian Broadcasting Corporation [FBC], where discussions were held on a proposed MoU with NBC covering digital broadcasting and archiving.

Other engagements included visits to the Fijian Government Data Centre, government digital infrastructure provider Walesi, and executives of Amalgamated Telecom Holdings/Vodafone.

Minister Naguri said he was encouraged by the level of cooperation shown during the visit and was keen to return to Fiji for the formal signing of the proposed MoU.

He was accompanied by Department of ICT Deputy Secretary for Policy Flierl Shongol and NBC Managing Director Kora Nou.

item.title: Minister backs Mauberema’s 10-year conservation effort
item.description: Environment, Conservation and Climate Change Minister John Kaupa has pledged government support for conservation and eco-tourism initiatives at Mauberema Ecotourism Lodge in Simbu Province. Minister Kaupa made a special visit to Mauberema on Saturday, October 31, following his absence from the official opening of the 7th Mauberema Show and 10th anniversary celebrations on Friday due to other offic
item.content:encoded:
Environment, Conservation and Climate Change Minister John Kaupa has pledged government support for conservation and eco-tourism initiatives at Mauberema Ecotourism Lodge in Simbu Province.

Minister Kaupa made a special visit to Mauberema on Saturday, October 31, following his absence from the official opening of the 7th Mauberema Show and 10th anniversary celebrations on Friday due to other official engagements in Western Highlands Provi

He was accompanied by the department’s First Assistant Secretary, Jack Ninkama, who commended the Mauberema community for its continued commitment to conservation and eco-tourism.

Mr Ninkama said the work being carried out at Mauberema reflected the type of conservation model the department wanted to see replicated across Papua New Guinea.

Minister Kaupa also commended local conservation champion Moses Kerry and his team for their dedication in sustaining conservation efforts over the past 10 years and successfully staging seven Mauberema Shows.

He said Mauberema stood alongside other national conservation models in Papua New Guinea.

The minister said his ministry, through the Climate Change and Development Authority [CCDA] and its development partners, would assist the community to further strengthen its conservation work.

He highlighted the importance of protecting forests to safeguard water sources, pointing to the continued availability of clean, fresh water for people in Dirima and communities along the road to Mauberema.

Minister Kaupa said he had known these communities since childhood and observed that their water supply had remained clean and abundant because of their efforts to protect the rainforest.

He described this as an example of effective conservation, declaring that the “Mauberema Way is the right way”.

Meanwhile, Mauberema is also attracting international research interest, with a PhD researcher currently studying birds and their behaviour in the local forest.

item.title: Court Sets Monday for Daru land ownership declaration
item.description: The Daru District Court has set Monday, November 2, for its final declaration on the customary ownership of Daru Town land, following a clarification session with all 49 clan leaders on Friday. Senior Provincial Magistrate for Daru, Robert Teko, said the court was now in the deliberation stage, carefully examining and verifying the narratives presented by the 49 clans against the historical backgr
item.content:encoded:
The Daru District Court has set Monday, November 2, for its final declaration on the customary ownership of Daru Town land, following a clarification session with all 49 clan leaders on Friday.

Senior Provincial Magistrate for Daru, Robert Teko, said the court was now in the deliberation stage, carefully examining and verifying the narratives presented by the 49 clans against the historical background of Daru Island to determine customary ownership.

"The court is now in the deliberation stage, where it is carefully examining and verifying each of the 49 clans' narratives against the historical background of Daru Island to determine customary ownership," Magistrate Teko said.

He said Friday’s session was held to explain the process being undertaken by the court and inform the clan leaders of the adjournment to Monday.

All 49 clan leaders attended the session, confirming full attendance.

The final declaration is scheduled for 9:30am on Monday, November 2, at the Daru District Court House.

Following Friday’s adjournment, clan leaders and their members left the courthouse peacefully, with no commotion reported.

Daru Town remained quiet and peaceful throughout Friday.

Western Provincial Administrator Robert Alphonse Kaiyun had earlier advised shops and business houses to close on Friday as a precautionary measure. They are expected to reopen today, Saturday, October 31.

A total liquor ban remains in effect under Circular No. 20 of 2026.

Combined security forces comprising the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary, PNG Defence Force and Correctional Service, together with ward law and order committees from around Daru Island, continue to maintain security.

The security operation is expected to continue until Wednesday, November 4.

Police have urged the public to remain calm, cooperate with security personnel and await the court’s official declaration on Monday.

item.title: New classroom boosts facilities at Hoskins Girls Technical School
item.description: Girls studying at Hoskins Girls Technical School in West New Britain Province will benefit from improved classroom facilities following the commissioning of a new double classroom. The K750,000 facility was funded by the National Department of Education under its infrastructure support programme.
item.content:encoded:
Girls studying at Hoskins Girls Technical School in West New Britain Province will benefit from improved classroom facilities following the commissioning of a new double classroom.

The K750,000 facility was funded by the National Department of Education under its infrastructure support programme.

Education Minister Francis Siune officially commissioned the new classroom at the school today, in the presence of West New Britain Governor Sasindran Muthuvel and Nakanai MP and Oil Palm Minister Francis Maneke.

Minister Siune said the facility was an investment in the education of girls in the province. He also acknowledged the school’s board and management for their role in securing the funding.

"This school is privileged to have benefitted from the Infrastructure grant given by the Department of Education in 2022 and this support is also a testimony of the competency of the board and management," he said.

He said the National Government remained focused on implementing education reforms, with the department continuing to invest in the capacity of education institutions to deliver the changes to the curriculum.

The minister said the reforms were also placing greater focus on technical and vocational education, as well as Flexible, Open and Distance Education (FODE) institutions.

Meanwhile, Governor Muthuvel and Minister Maneke acknowledged the Department of Education’s support and called for more partnerships to improve education infrastructure in the province.

item.title: New facilities bring service closer to Menyamya locals
item.description: The people of Menyamya now have new public facilities in their district, including a government office complex, police station, market facilities and a water supply project. Prime Minister James Marape officially opened the facilities yesterday, alongside a refurbished rural lock-up.
item.content:encoded:
The people of Menyamya now have new public facilities in their district, including a government office complex, police station, market facilities and a water supply project.

Prime Minister James Marape officially opened the facilities yesterday, alongside a refurbished rural lock-up.

For years, some locals have described Menyamya as the “back page”, highlighting the challenges of accessing government services and basic infrastructure.

The new district office complex, which cost about K14.7 million, was built under a contract awarded to Pioneer Construction and Engineering Limited.

Having government office facilities in the district provides a base for public administration closer to local communities. The services available to locals will depend on which government agencies operate from the complex.

The market facilities provide a designated place for farmers and vendors to sell their produce and other goods, supporting local trading activities.

For families who depend on selling garden produce for income, access to a market is an important part of earning a living. The benefits will depend on how the facility is used by vendors and buyers.

The water supply project includes Southern Cross tanks, adding to Menyamya's water infrastructure. The number of people who will have access to the supply and the project's total cost were not available.

A new police station and refurbished rural lock-up also form part of the developments, providing facilities for police operations in the district.

The projects address different community needs, from government administration and local trading to water infrastructure and policing.

For Menyamya locals, the value of these facilities will be measured by the services they can access, the opportunities available to local vendors and the practical use of the water and police infrastructure.

The opening marks a new stage for the district, with the focus now on how the facilities operate and serve communities across Menyamya.
